        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x

            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve

$ go test  # ladder-a
    the column parse is owned by . and ./b, each as a lift. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename one of the lifts, or remove one. Of . and ./b, which own the lift, one that only reads its product removes its column by giving the lift to hypercase.Use in place of hypercase.Own.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/evaluate
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
FAIL
[exit 1]

$ go test  # ladder-a-useonly
    the lift parse is used by . and ./b, and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere.
        Own the lift in one of them: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
    testdata/script/x.txtar: no registry claims out/parse/outcome: no column named parse runs over the corpus script.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, run hypercase strip -column parse at the module root, then FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... until it changes nothing. The strip removes parse's sections from every archive under the module-root corpus, and the update writes back each one a registry claims, but not one whose cell the update writes nothing for, such as a cell that faults.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/evaluate
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
FAIL
[exit 1]

$ go test  # ladder-a
    the column outline is owned by ./b and ./c, each as a suite. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename one of the suites, or remove one.
    the column parse is owned by ., ./b and ./c, each as a lift. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename or remove all but one of the lifts. Of ., ./b and ./c, which own the lift, one that only reads its product removes its column by giving the lift to hypercase.Use in place of hypercase.Own.

        parse ran on x
